Aisha (arch): Heads-up 1: we need a practical escape hatch for the streaming frame migration (v1 -> v2 frames). Clients using old framed-chunks will break once we switch runtime serializers. Proposal: edge-level shim that rewrites incoming v1 frames to v2 and rewrites outgoing v2->v1 for flagged tenants. This keeps runtime unchanged. Thoughts?
Jen (eng-platform): sounds good for hosted. how do we gate who gets rewrite? feature flag header? tenant opt-in?
Marco (eng-runtime): two concerns: 1) correctness: framing semantics differ for EOF vs mid-stream errors; 2) perf: double-encode/decode in edge adds CPU and latency. We should only rewrite for a small cohort.
Omar (eng-infra): envoy filter can do streaming transformation but needs to be careful with backpressure. We already have a few filters that mutate the body in-flight. We could implement a streaming Lua filter or a WASM filter for efficiency.
Aisha (arch): decision criteria: rewriting at edge is preferred because it avoids touching hot runtime path. We'll implement a WASM filter that translates wire frames. Gate by header `X-RW-Frame-Compat: v1` (signed token for safety).
Jen (eng-platform): how to prevent spoofing? Use HMAC with tenant secret, like `X-RW-Frame-Compat: v1:hmactok`. Auth service issues short-lived proofs during rollout.
Marco (eng-runtime): also need to record `compat.format=v1` in spans so we can track regressions. Also, when a tenant is served via shim, mark their KV caches appropriately because frame rewrite may change streaming boundaries we rely on.
Aisha (arch): good point. Cache key plan: include `frame_compat` tag: `cache_key = tenant + ':' + frame_compat + ':' + key`. If we can't change existing keys for archived caches, add a migration TTL to avoid collisions.
Omar (eng-infra): private/air-gapped customers: they may not accept our envoy filter. Offer two options: 1) deploy our WASM filter via their control plane; 2) runtime-side adapter (sidecar) they install. Document both, but prefer envoy route for hosted.
Jen (eng-platform): rollout plan suggestion: a) internal infra tenants b) 1% random tenants for 48h c) targeted customers (low-latency) d) open opt-in. Abort if 5xx rate increases by >1% or stream integrity checks fail.
sre-bot: Added alert `streaming-frame-rewrite:error_rate` threshold 1% for canary cohorts.
Marco (eng-runtime): test harness: add fuzz tests for frame conversions and cross-compat scenario (v1 client <-> v2 runtime and vice versa). Also validate chunk boundaries and EOL semantics.
Aisha (arch): will we ever remove the shim? long-term: once majority move to v2, schedule shim sunset with 90 day notice and telemetry-backed thresholds.
Jen (eng-platform): need admin override in console for support to toggle shim per-tenant. Must be auditable. Also expose metric `requests_frame_compat{version="v1"}`.
Omar (eng-infra): implementation tasks: WASM filter PoC (Omar), HMAC header flow + auth support (Jen), runtime cache namespacing + metrics (Marco), tests + CI harness (Marco/Jen).
Marco (eng-runtime): minor runtime change: accept `runtime.headers.migrated=true` from edge metadata, but we won't parse frames in runtime. fallback flag if edge indicates rewrite failed.
Aisha (arch): docs: platform playbook for private deploys, deprecation timeline, and SDK notes for clients to add header during opt-in.
Jen (eng-platform): example curl for testing:
``
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "X-RW-Frame-Compat: v1:abcd-signature" \
     -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/generate
```
Omar (eng-infra): I'll prototype a WASM filter this week. tagging infra-wo.
Aisha (arch): thanks all. follow-up sync next Tue with PoC results. :white_check_mark:
